title: Silently crash on GetQuotaObjectForFile
body: I am using 64-bit Firefox 115.0.2 on Windows 7 SP1. While uploading 16 videos totaling about 64 GB to YouTube in Private Browsing, Firefox silently crashes after a while. There is no crash reporter window and about:crashes has no recent entry. Restarting and retrying produces the same crash; Firefox 114 did not have this issue. I disabled HTTP/3 to get full upload speed. WinDbg consistently shows access violation 0xc0000005 in xul.dll at mozilla::storage::GetQuotaObjectForFile, QuotaVFS.cpp line 616, while dereferencing what looks like invalid memory. Process Explorer is always running, and I do not know whether that interferes with crash reporting. I primarily want the browser crash fixed.

symptoms_visible: While I upload many large videos to YouTube in Private Browsing, Firefox 115.0.2 silently closes after a while.
No crash reporter window appears, and about:crashes contains no recent crash.
WinDbg repeatedly stops on a 0xc0000005 access violation in xul.dll at GetQuotaObjectForFile.
N0.label: N0 silent upload crash reported

symptoms_visible: During a large upload, a child process can grow to around 17 GB and then repeatedly drop and regain several gigabytes while network transfer stops.
When I attach WinDbg to the active process, it catches an invalid-memory access in GetQuotaObjectForFile on an IndexedDB thread.
The crash still occurs after Firefox switches to 115.0.2 ESR.
N1.label: N1 debugger capture and memory behavior collected

symptoms_visible: In a clean Firefox 115.0.3 ESR profile, two normal-browsing batches of fifteen 2 GB videos complete without a crash.
With the same profile and files in Private Browsing, Firefox crashes while beginning the sixth file.
N2.label: N2 private-browsing isolation reproduced

symptoms_visible: The crash happens with about 10.4 GB still free on the system drive, and immediately afterward free space rises to about 14.4 GB.
The Private Browsing IndexedDB files total about 9.9 GB after five videos; when the sixth upload starts, another file appears briefly, disappears, and Firefox crashes seconds later.
N3.label: N3 quota-boundary file behavior observed

symptoms_visible: In a build containing the storage fix, a large Private Browsing upload can pass the previous approximately 10 GB boundary without the whole browser closing in GetQuotaObjectForFile.
N_terminal.label: terminal storage cast fixed

question_patterns: What happens to Firefox memory and network activity before the crash?
Do you see unusual process memory growth or an upload stall before Firefox closes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Usually a child process leaks memory. When it reaches about 17 GB, the upload can stop transferring bytes and memory just drops by a few GB and grows back again. In Firefox 114 the tab could crash from overflowing RAM, but in 115 the whole browser can suddenly close.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Memory stays flat and the browser crashes immediately when I select the first file, before any upload data is buffered.

question_patterns: Can you attach WinDbg to the active Firefox process and capture the faulting thread and stack?
What does the debugger show at the moment of the crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Starting Firefox under WinDbg watched only an empty stub process, so I attached to the active process instead. That catches an access to unallocated memory at GetQuotaObjectForFile+0x15. The stack is on an 'IndexedDB #46' thread and goes through Connection::GetQuotaObjects and StartTransactionOp::DoDatabaseWork.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The attached debugger catches an out-of-memory termination on the main thread, with no IndexedDB or GetQuotaObjectForFile frames.
The IndexedDB thread number differs, but the fault and the GetQuotaObjectForFile stack are the same.

question_patterns: Does the crash still reproduce after the switch to Firefox 115 ESR?
Which current Firefox build still shows the crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Firefox switched itself to 115.0.2 ESR. The crash is still there in the same function; only the xul.dll offset changed because it is a different binary.

edges.comment: The reporter supplied memory behavior and a full attached-debugger stack after the opening report. The later 115.0.2 ESR installation is a persistent system change, so the target uses a new system_state_id.

question_patterns: Can you repeat the same upload in a clean profile using normal browsing rather than Private Browsing?
Does an equivalent large upload complete outside Private Browsing?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I started a clean profile, with the significant change that HTTP/3 is disabled. I uploaded thirty 2 GB videos in normal browsing, fifteen per batch, and all of them completed without a crash.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The clean-profile normal-browsing upload crashes on the sixth file in exactly the same way.

question_patterns: Now can you try those same files in Private Browsing and report where the crash occurs?
Is the failure specifically reproducible in a private window?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the same clean profile and files in Private Browsing, Firefox crashes when it tries to upload the sixth 2 GB file out of the first batch of fifteen.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: All fifteen files also complete in Private Browsing, so I cannot reproduce the crash in either mode.
It crashes on the seventh file rather than the sixth, but only in Private Browsing at roughly the same stored size.

question_patterns: Which Firefox version did you use for the controlled normal-versus-private comparison?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced the comparison on Firefox 115.0.3 ESR. The private run crashes with 0xc0000005 in xul.dll; the normal run completes.

edges.comment: The handler's Private Browsing question led to controlled clean-profile comparisons. Firefox 115.0.3 ESR was installed before these tests, which creates another persistent system state.

question_patterns: How much free space remains on the system drive before and after the crash?
Can you check whether the system disk is actually full when the private upload fails?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I initially had 20.3 GB free. In another run there was 10.4 GB free shortly before the crash, and immediately after the crash it showed 14.4 GB free. The crash happens before the system drive runs out of space.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The system drive reaches zero free bytes before every crash and remains full afterward.
There is about 12 GB free before the crash and about 15 GB afterward; it still fails near the same private-storage size.

question_patterns: Did these large uploads work in Private Browsing on Firefox versions before 115, or only in normal browsing?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: They worked in Private Browsing before Firefox 115. There could be crashes from overflowing RAM, but this repeatable whole-browser crash at the storage boundary is new in 115.

edges.comment: Disk-space checking was a handler-initiated measurement. The reporter then independently inspected the private IndexedDB directory and volunteered that five files total about 9.9 GB and the sixth file briefly appears and is removed before the crash.

solution.intent: Fix GetQuotaObjectForFile so it does not statically cast an ObfuscatingVFS-backed sqlite file as a QuotaVFS file when encrypted Private Browsing IndexedDB reaches its quota path, and ask the reporter to verify a build containing the landed fix with the same large private upload.
solution.concrete_example: Private Browsing IndexedDB wraps QuotaVFS with ObfuscatingVFS. GetQuotaObjectForFile incorrectly assumed the sqlite3_file was directly the QuotaVFS file and used a static cast, so the quota path dereferenced the wrong object near the 10 GB group limit. Replace that cast with VFS-aware access or forwarding through ObfuscatingVFS, add coverage for this private-browsing path, and then ask: 'Please retest the same upload in today's fixed build and tell me whether it passes the previous boundary without closing Firefox.'
solution.inference_hint: The reporter observed a GetQuotaObjectForFile access violation, private-only reproduction, and files reaching about 9.9 GB. Engineers inferred that Private Browsing IndexedDB uses ObfuscatingVFS over QuotaVFS, that the 10 GB group limit enters quota handling, and that GetQuotaObjectForFile's static cast treats the wrapper as the underlying QuotaVFS file. Those conclusions must not be placed in the user's raw answers.

edges.comment: Engineering identified the wrong static cast in QuotaVFS.cpp and landed the fix as mozilla-central revisions b267fb9e2882 and f8a705dd9062. The thread contains no reporter retest after landing, so a matching answer must request verification and must not claim that the reporter already confirmed the fixed build.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: Private Browsing IndexedDB uses ObfuscatingVFS over QuotaVFS, but GetQuotaObjectForFile performed a static cast that only works when IndexedDB uses QuotaVFS directly, causing an invalid dereference when the private quota path was exercised.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the IndexedDB-thread WinDbg stack, normal-versus-private clean-profile comparison, approximately 9.9 GB of private IndexedDB files, disappearance of the sixth file, and remaining system disk space.
Must fix the VFS handling or forwarding rather than treating system disk exhaustion, Process Explorer, or the missing crash reporter as the cause of the browser crash.
Must not present the reporter's speculation about a freed file or object as established fact; the confirmed engineering defect is the wrong cast involving ObfuscatingVFS and QuotaVFS.

Must ask the reporter to verify the same large Private Browsing upload on a build containing the fix before declaring user-confirmed resolution; the original thread contains no post-fix reporter verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical power user who can attach WinDbg, inspect registers and native stacks, monitor process memory, inspect profile storage files, and run controlled large-upload comparisons, but does not know the internal VFS wrapper design.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent, direct, and evidence-heavy; reports exact versions, offsets, file sizes, free-space readings, and repeated reproduction steps, while clearly distinguishing guesses from observations.
